steps.name: Load counts, validate metadata, QC and batch check
caveats: counts.csv is salmon output; if values are decimal estimated counts, DESeq2 needs rounding (or tximport) — record which was done and its effect
The 13th column of counts.csv is presumably a gene identifier column — verify rownames before matching
12,000 genes is fewer than a full transcriptome — note whether this is a pre-filtered matrix
steps.question: Are the 12 samples in counts.csv and metadata.csv consistent and suitable for a ~batch+condition model, and does batch structure dominate or obscure the treated-vs-control signal in unsupervised views (PCA, sample distances)?
constraints: Read-only on input files; write all outputs to the step's own output directory
Do not apply batch correction (e.g. ComBat or removeBatchEffect on counts) — batch is handled in the design matrix downstream
Report integer-ness check result explicitly before any transformation
steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-v2-without-batch-balanced-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples + ID column) and metadata.csv (12 rows x 3 cols: sample id, condition, batch). Validate that sample names match 1:1 between files, establish whether counts are integers or decimal salmon estimated counts (if non-integer, round for DESeq2 and record this), and inspect identifier type (gene symbol vs Ensembl vs Entrez). Filter low-abundance genes (keep genes with >=10 counts in a minimal number of samples per DESeq2 convention) and report how many of 12,000 remain. Produce PCA on variance-stabilized values colored by condition and by batch, and a sample-to-sample distance heatmap, to characterize treatment signal and batch structure before modeling.
acceptance_criteria: All 12 samples present in both counts and metadata with 1:1 matching; any mismatch reported, not silently dropped
Count matrix integer-ness established and the handling of salmon estimated counts documented in output
PCA and sample-distance plots produced colored by condition and by batch; batch effect magnitude qualitatively assessed
Gene filtering counts (in 12,000 -> kept) reported

steps.name: Differential expression: DESeq2 ~batch + condition
caveats: With n=6 vs 6 and one batch covariate, dispersion estimates rest on ~10 residual df — expect wide CIs and treat FDR-threshold gene lists as candidate-level
Handle all-zero / non-converging genes explicitly and report counts
Verify the DESeq2 1.52 lfcShrink API (contrast= or coef= usage with apeglm type) before calling
steps.question: Which genes differ between treated and control after accounting for the two processing batches (DESeq2 design ~ batch + condition, contrast treated vs control), and how much does the batch adjustment change the result versus ignoring batch?
constraints: Condition and batch factors must both enter the design; the DE contrast itself is treated vs control, never batch
Use apeglm type LFC shrinkage for reporting effect sizes; keep the unshrunk Wald statistic for the fgsea ranking
Do not drop samples or add covariates beyond batch without documenting it
steps.description: Run DESeq2 (DESeqDataSetFromMatrix) with design ~ batch + condition on the filtered count matrix from T1S1, factor levels set so control is the reference and the contrast is treated vs control. Wald test, independent filtering, BH adjustment. Apply apeglm LFC shrinkage for reporting effect sizes. Also fit the reduced model ~ condition (no batch term) purely as a sensitivity analysis: report how many genes are significant in each and the overlap, so the cost/benefit of batch adjustment is visible. Save the full results table (gene, baseMean, shrunk log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) plus a record of dispersion and size-factor summaries.
acceptance_criteria: Fitted model is ~ batch + condition with treated vs control as the reference-coded contrast
Results table with baseMean, log2FoldChange (apeglm-shrunk), lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj for all tested genes saved as TSV
Number of genes at FDR<0.05 (and at FDR<0.05 & |LFC|>1) reported with adjusted-p distribution summary
Sensitivity comparison (with vs without batch term) quantified: counts of significant genes in each and their overlap

steps.name: DE visualization: volcano, MA, heatmap
caveats: Only 12 samples and ~10k genes post-filter: heatmaps of the top 25-50 genes are informative; whole-transcriptome heatmaps are not
Check EnhancedVolcano argument names against its current API before plotting
steps.question: What does the treated-vs-control result look like at a glance: effect sizes, significance structure, and whether top genes separate by condition or by batch?
constraints: Label points using whatever identifier type the count matrix carries (established in T1S1)
Keep axes and thresholds consistent with T1S2 definitions (padj, shrunk LFC)
steps.description: Produce the standard DE figure set from T1S2 outputs: (1) volcano plot of shrunk LFC vs -log10(padj) with FDR<0.05 genes highlighted and top genes labeled (EnhancedVolcano), (2) MA plot, (3) heatmap of variance-stabilized values for the top 25-50 significant genes with condition and batch annotation bars (pheatmap), (4) sample-to-sample distance heatmap if not already saved in T1S1. All figures written to disk as PNG/PDF.
acceptance_criteria: Volcano plot (shrunk LFC vs -log10 padj) with significant genes highlighted and gene labels for top hits
MA plot of the ~batch+condition fit
Heatmap of variance-stabilized values for top significant genes with condition and batch annotations
All figures written as files; no figures left in memory only

steps.name: Pathway enrichment: FGSEA on WikiPathways human
caveats: WikiPathways gene symbols are HGNC; identifier-space mismatch between counts and GMT is the most likely silent failure — check coverage before interpreting
Build rankings from the Wald statistic of the ~batch+condition fit; do not use the no-batch fit for the primary enrichment
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes shifted in treated vs control, after batch adjustment, and do the over-representation and ranking-based views agree?
constraints: Use the human GMT only — the dataset is Homo sapiens; never substitute the staged rat/mouse pathway files
Resolve the human WikiPathways GMT against /mnt/refs at run time via list_available_refs; if absent, report the step could not run rather than guessing a path

Map identifiers: if the count matrix uses Ensembl or Entrez IDs rather than HGNC symbols, convert via the staged human UniProt id-mapping table (col 3 GeneID, col 19 Ensembl) or org.Hs.eg.db, and report mapping coverage
steps.description: Run gene-set enrichment on the treated-vs-control signal: (1) FGSEA preranked with the human WikiPathways GMT staged under /mnt/refs (wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt, HGNC symbols), ranking all tested genes by the Wald statistic (or sign(stat)*-log10 p) from the ~batch+condition fit; (2) over-representation analysis (fgsea::fora or clusterProfiler enricher) on the FDR<0.05 gene list. Parse the '%'-delimited GMT descriptor for readable pathway names. Report top enriched pathways with NES and adjusted p-values.
acceptance_criteria: FGSEA run on the full ranked list (all tested genes); NES and padj per pathway saved
ORA on FDR<0.05 significant genes saved alongside with overlapping-gene lists
Top pathways (padj<0.25 or top 20 by padj) written to disk with pathway names parsed from the GMT descriptor
Mapping coverage of dataset genes against GMT members reported

steps.name: Consolidated DE report
caveats: 6 vs 6 with one batch covariate: effect-size CIs are wide; phrase conclusions as candidate findings
If enrichment mapping coverage was low (<50%), flag pathway results as incomplete rather than exhaustive
steps.question: What genes and pathways differ between treated and control in this kidney bulk RNA-seq dataset, and with what caveats about batch handling, count provenance, and power (n=6 vs 6)?
constraints: Distinguish observation (DE table, enrichment tables) from interpretation (pathway narratives) in the summary
Carry the n=12 small-sample caveat and the salmon-counts provenance caveat into the report text
steps.description: Write one consolidated summary tying the run together: the authoritative DE table reference (~batch + condition, apeglm-shrunk), top 10 up and top 10 down genes by shrunk LFC among FDR-significant genes, the batch-sensitivity comparison (significant-gene counts and overlap with vs without the batch term), the top FGSEA pathways with NES/padj, and the explicit caveats recorded during the run (salmon estimated counts handling, gene-filter fraction, identifier mapping coverage, n=6 vs 6 statistical power).
acceptance_criteria: Single summary document (markdown) written to the run output directory
Report leads with the actual numbers: n genes FDR<0.05, top 10 by padj/LFC, top 10 pathways by FGSEA padj, with/without-batch overlap
Stated explicitly: which model is authoritative (~batch + condition), what was rounded/filtered, and the small-sample caveat
No result cited in the summary that is not present in a saved artifact

plan.title: Batch-adjusted DE: kidney treated vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are gene-level counts from salmon (12,000 genes x 12 samples in counts.csv) with a 12-row metadata table (sample, condition, batch). Design is 6 treated vs 6 control with two processing batches, each holding both conditions, so batch and condition are crossed and both can be estimated in one model. The analysis runs a DESeq2 Wald test with the design ~ batch + condition, applies apeglm LFC shrinkage, and compares against a no-batch design as a sensitivity check so the effect of adjusting for batch is explicit rather than assumed. Because the counts are salmon-derived and the profile does not state whether length correction was applied, the load step must first establish whether values are integers or decimal estimated counts and record how this was handled (rounding per DESeq2 documented practice) before any inference. Downstream: QC (PCA, sample distances, batch check), differential expression with batch adjustment, publication-standard visualizations, and FGSEA enrichment against the staged WikiPathways Homo sapiens GMT using the DE ranked statistics, plus an over-representation check on the FDR-significant gene set.
